basics.name: Luke Zhu
basics.label: Mathematics & Physics, Harvard College
basics.summary: Undergraduate at Harvard College double majoring in Mathematics (Honors) and Physics, with a concurrent A.M. in Mathematics. Research interests in algebra, geometry, and topology, particularly applications to quantum error correction and topological data analysis.

education.area: A.B. in Mathematics (Honors) and Physics; A.M. in Mathematics (Concurrent)
Visiting Student, Oriel College; Mathematical Institute

highlights: Lead weekly office hours and recitation sessions to improve student understanding
Grade student assignments, helping students improve rigour and exposition
Lead academic content design for nationwide mathematics and physics competitions
Design novel problems requiring physical intuition and creative quantitative reasoning

projects.name: Harvard Honors Thesis
projects.description: Research in quantum stabilizer codes (a mathematical framework for error correction in quantum computers) through algebraic and topological interpretations. Advised by Bowen Yang at Harvard's CMSA.

projects.name: Affine Group Schemes
projects.description: Studying affine group schemes and commutative Hopf algebras with a view towards generalising the theory to symmetric monoidal categories. Advised by Professor Kobi Kremnitzer at Oxford.

projects.name: Machine Learning for Knot Theory
projects.description: Received Harvard funding to research applications of machine learning in knot theory, with applications to invariant prediction, classification tasks, and biopolymer identification.

projects.name: HARDMATH2 (NeurIPS 2025)
projects.description: Developed benchmark tasks for evaluating LLM performance on applied mathematics problems, with emphasis on multi-step modeling, quantitative reasoning, and solution verification.

projects.name: ETG x NASA VECAR Project
projects.description: Collaborated with NASA's Volatiles Extraction Cryocapture & Recovery project, designing a lunar-capable device to extract and return soil volatiles to Earth via the Artemis program.

volunteer.summary: Volunteer for HSHS on weekends, working breakfast and evening shifts.

Teacher for the CMC, a 501(c)3 registered nonprofit that delivers maths enrichment to K-8 students from Cambridge and the Greater Boston area, with a focus on children commonly underrepresented in STEM.
